chunks: From him, from a number of our companions, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, raising it, said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who is pleased from the world with whatever his apportionment is, the least of what is in it would suffice him; and the one who is not pleased from the world with what his apportionment is, there is nothing in it which would suffice him'.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: His apportioned share / what suffices him

ai.seo_question: How does contentment affect one's perception of sufficiency in the world according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of *rida* (contentment) as the true measure of wealth, emphasizing that spiritual satisfaction with Allah's decree (*qismah*) renders even a small share sufficient. It contrasts this inner peace with the insatiable greed of the dissatisfied, who find no comfort in abundance, a theme deeply rooted in the sermons of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the transient nature of worldly life.
